description: We are a multidisciplinary team of Biomedical Engineering students and researchers from Ecuador (Universidad Politécnica Salesiana / IEEE EMBS) tackling the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge. Our core strengths include biomedical signal processing, physiological data analysis, Python, MATLAB, and software development. We are building a clinical telemetry and anomaly-detection dashboard powered by open NASA physiological datasets.
summary: A.S.T.R.A.-Bio is a 100% offline Edge Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) powered by an adaptive N-of-1 physiological digital twin for deep-space missions. In altered gravity, high radiation, and closed habitats, fixed terrestrial thresholds trigger frequent false alarms during fluid-shift acclimation and fail to catch multi-system decompensation early. By combining phase-aware Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) individual baselines with a Multi-System Coupling Index (MSCI), A.S.T.R.A.-Bio couples cabin environmental telemetry (solar radiation, ppCO2) with astronaut biomarkers (HRV RMSSD, sleep efficiency, core temp, ARED compliance). Across a reproducible 30-seed Monte Carlo simulation of a 60-day mission, A.S.T.R.A.-Bio reduces Days 1–14 acclimation false alarms by 84.8% (mean 1.0 vs. 6.6) and detects a Day-42 Solar Particle Event (SPE) decompensation +42.5 hours early (range 38–46h), prescribing closed-loop onboard countermeasures during 22-minute Mars communication blackouts.
details:
Live Offline-Capable Web Application: https://gleeful-eclair-3d2036.netlify.app/

Open-Source GitHub Repository: https://github.com/bemg04martinez-droid/astra-bio-nasa-2026

PROBLEM & DEEP-SPACE AUTONOMY GAP:

During lunar and Martian missions, communication delays of up to 22 minutes each way (44 minutes round-trip) and solar conjunction blackouts prevent real-time Earth-based medical intervention. Meanwhile, static terrestrial clinical cutoffs fail in microgravity: cephalad fluid shifts during Days 1–14 cause benign autonomic fluctuations that trigger false alarms, while subtle multi-system interactions (elevated ppCO2, solar radiation, sleep fragmentation, and HRV suppression) go undetected until acute clinical decompensation occurs.

ARCHITECTURE & N-OF-1 DIGITAL TWIN ENGINE:

A.S.T.R.A.-Bio runs 100% client-side (React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, custom SVG telemetry engine) with zero cloud dependencies, allowing onboard execution during Earth-link blackouts:

1. Phase-Aware N-of-1 EWMA Engine: Continuously adapts individual physiological baselines using dynamic smoothing factors (lambda = 0.28 during Days 1–14 microgravity acclimatization, lambda = 0.12 during nominal cruise, and anomaly-gated freezing lambda = 0.02 during acute events to prevent baseline drift).

2. Multi-System Coupling Index (MSCI): Computes directional z-scores across autonomic (HRV RMSSD, resting HR, core temperature), environmental (GCR/SPE radiation dose rate, cabin ppCO2), circadian (sleep efficiency), and musculoskeletal (ARED resistive load compliance and SANS risk) streams, capturing non-linear cross-system synergy.

3. Explainable AI (XAI) & Closed-Loop Protocols: Dynamically decomposes the MSCI into real-time causal attribution bars (52% Autonomic vagal suppression, 27% Circadian & CO2 stress, 17% Solar radiation exposure, 4% Bone deconditioning during the Day-42 SPE) and maps actionable countermeasures to spacecraft subsystems (ECLSS/CDRA high-flow CO2 scrubbing, storm shelter shielding, ARED eccentric load auto-throttling, LBNP, and 480 nm SSLA circadian lighting).

4. Objective Micro-Assessments & Store-and-Forward Telemetry: Includes a built-in 0.1 Hz Resonant Breathing Biofeedback Pacer and a 15-second Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) alongside compressed FHIR-Lite JSON telemetry bundles queued for asynchronous Earth downlink.

REPRODUCIBLE 30-SEED BENCHMARK:

Evaluated across 30 deterministic Monte Carlo seeds (Mulberry32 PRNG) over a 60-day mission, A.S.T.R.A.-Bio cuts Days 1–14 microgravity fluid-shift false alarms from a mean of 6.6 (range 3–11) under fixed Earth thresholds down to 1.0 (range 0–2)—an 84.8% reduction in alarm fatigue. During the injected Day-42 Solar Particle Event (SPE), the coupled MSCI model achieves a mean early detection lead time of +42.5 hours (range 38–46h) ahead of static clinical cutoffs.
